references.text: Aaron stretches out his hand with the staff to perform a sign, just as he does here when dust turns into gnats.
Aaron stretches out his hand with the staff to bring a plague upon Egypt, in the same way as with the gnat plague.
The Lord's command to Moses that Aaron should strike the dust with the staff, which is carried out here.
The psalm describes how God spoke and flies and gnats came throughout their land, a poetic retelling of this plague.
Another plague where dust is used as an instrument—Moses throws ashes toward the sky, which become boils on people and animals.
The magicians try to do the same with their sorcery but fail and acknowledge that this is the finger of God.
Both plagues involve a direct transformation of the earth's dust into an instrument of judgment (gnats/boils) against people and animals.
